title: Unveiling [C II] clumps in a lensed star-forming galaxy at z ∼ 3.4
question: Are there [C II]-emitting clumps (parent molecular clouds) in a lensed z~3.4 galaxy that hosts UV clumps, and what are their gas masses and depletion times?

data.sensitivity: 0.03 mJy/beam continuum over 4811 km/s; 0.20 mJy/beam over 102 km/s

what.value: Lens model and magnifications (mu = 5.5±0.7 for M1, 4.5±0.3 for M2)

evidence.loc: 2.1 Our target galaxy and ancillary data
evidence.quote: The average lensing magnification of M1 and M2 is $\mu = 5.5 \pm 0.7$ and $\mu = 4.5 \pm 0.3$, respectively

what.value: [C II] luminosity-to-gas mass conversion alpha_[CII] = 31 Msun/Lsun (0.3 dex scatter)

evidence.quote: $\mathrm{\alpha_{[C\,{\footnotesize II}]}} = 31\, \mathrm{M_\odot/L_\odot}$ (with a scatter of 0.3 dex) as estimated by (cite: Zanella2018)

what.value: UV slope beta = -2.53 ± 0.15 and E(B-V)_cont < 0.16 mag

evidence.quote: blue $\beta = -2.53 \pm 0.15$ slope of the galaxy as estimated from the rest-frame UV spectrum (cite: Iani2021)

what.value: Literature sub-galactic regions of z~1-4 galaxies for the Schmidt-Kennicutt plane

evidence.loc: 5.1 Gas depletion time and Schmidt-Kennicutt plane
evidence.quote: compares it with literature galaxies and their subkiloparsec regions (cite: Freundlich2013; Hodge2015; Nagy2023; Bethermin2023)

recipe.goal: Model UV continuum of HST image
recipe.method: GALFIT Sérsic diffuse component plus PSF/Sérsic clump components; BCG subtracted; fluxes divided by magnification

recipe.goal: Extract [C II] line and integrated map
recipe.method: Iterative uv-plane 2D Gaussian fit (uv_fit) channel by channel, extract 1D spectrum, average best channels, refit position until convergence
Averaged line-free channels; 5σ upper limit from uv-plane Gaussian or PSF fit with fixed position
Natural-weighted channel maps; ≥4σ peaks within 1/3 primary beam with >3σ overlapping emission in ≥2 adjacent 20.3 km/s channels
uv-plane fit of 2D PSF per channel with free centre (method 3), summed over adjacent channels; compared to image-plane and Gaussian fits; corrected by average magnification

recipe.goal: Compute SFR and molecular gas mass
recipe.method: SFR from UV 1500Å luminosity (Kennicutt98, Chabrier IMF); Mmol = alpha_[CII] × L_[CII] with alpha = 31 Msun/Lsun
assumptions: No dust correction of UV; [C II] emission mostly from molecular gas

recipe.method: PV diagrams and moment maps with immoments (2.5σ threshold); Jeans length from sigma and Sigma_gas
assumptions: Rotation contribution to dispersion neglected; sigma ~20 km/s

recipe.method: t_dep = Sigma_mol/Sigma_SFR compared to literature at ~400 pc radius

evidence.quote: The total observed flux is $\mathrm{F_{[C\,{\footnotesize II}]} = 7.5 \pm 0.7\, mJy}$ (over $\mathrm{\Delta v = 122\, km\, s^{-1}}$).
$\mathrm{F_{cont} < 34\, \mu Jy}$ when considering a PSF model

answer_key.quantity: SW and C clump depletion time

evidence.quote: we obtain gravitationally unstable scales $\mathrm{\lambda_J \sim 100\, pc}$

answer_key.quantity: Probability of noise peaks mimicking symmetric NE clump

evidence.quote: with a symmetric position (e.g., being in the N-E side of the galaxy) to be 0.08%

not_stated_but_needed: Line-free channel ranges used for the continuum map
Exact uv_fit/imaging settings (cell size, image size, uv taper) in GILDAS
Absolute flux calibration uncertainty and phase calibrators
Full details of the lens model and magnification maps (from Iani2021)
Kennicutt UV-SFR conversion constants after IMF scaling
Area definition used for the surface densities of clumps
Number of ALMA antennas and array configuration
missing_for_reproduction: Lens model and magnification maps from Iani2021
HST data reduction and Kennicutt conversion details
score_reason: Public data and a fairly clear recipe but low-S/N clump detection, GILDAS-specific fitting and inherited lens model make exact reproduction difficult.
rediscovery_reason: Public single-project data, numeric results (flux, redshift, gas mass, t_dep), though some inherited inputs are needed.
